data.note:
Note for dossier:

Unblinded as mevinolin / lovastatin, PubChem CID 53232, ChEMBL CHEMBL503 HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (e23), BBBC021 Cholesterol-lowering. My blinded calls (Microtubule stabilizers, revised to Actin disruptors) were both incorrect.

What misled: 1.5-5 uM replicated actin condensation, contraction, multinucleate proxy with actin-like atlas (e13, e20 top cytochalasin B 0.90), and 15 uM bundled tubulin with 7/10 MT-stabilizer neighbours (e14) drove MT-stabilizer call. I discounted the Cholesterol-lowering neighbours present in the same lists (simvastatin e13, e20).

Literature now explains the mimicry: statins block prenylation-dependent actin regulation (PMID:1560030), prevent RhoA activation (PMID:16774905), and act via Rho-dependent mechanisms (PMID:11487529). So cholesterol-lowering can phenocopy actin disruptors secondarily, which is the class lesson to retain.

reflection.text:
I over-weighted the toxic high-dose acquisitions: the 15uM well with only 69 cells showing tub_glcm_contrast z=+66.8 together with act_glcm_contrast z=+41.7, and the combined 5+15uM atlas match to Microtubule stabilizers 7/10, and treated simultaneous tubulin and actin texture elevation as fibrillar bundling rather than contraction artifact. The reviewer critique was correct that p=0.62 was uncalibrated because the mitotic signal was weak at rho=+0.60 p=0.4 and the intermediate-dose signal did not independently support stabilizers.

What pointed the right way was the replicated mid-dose phenotype I under-weighted: 1.5uM rep1 and rep2 both showed actin-dominant texture with multinucleation and low mitotic activity, the 1.5uM-alone atlas had Actin disruptors 3/10 with zero Microtubule stabilizer neighbours, and the requested single-well 5uM atlas returned Actin disruptors 4/10 with Cholesterol-lowering 2/10. The 50uM well with nuc_solidity z=-192.5 should have further warned that high-dose nuclear collapse was driving texture scores.

I missed Cholesterol-lowering because I did not include it in the hypothesis set until after review and did not interpret actin disruption as statin pleiotropy via prenylation and Rho signaling rather than direct actin or tubulin binding.
what_was_right: Flagged strong dose-dependent cytoskeletal remodeling with tub_mean and act_mean both rho=+1.00 and replicated actin texture plus multinucleation at 1.5uM across e2 and e16
Noted low cell count at 15uM with 69 cells and extreme parallel tubulin and actin z-scores, consistent with toxicity and contraction
Post-review single-well 5uM atlas e20 correctly surfaced Cholesterol-lowering 2/10 alongside Actin disruptors 4/10
what_was_wrong: Submitted Microtubule stabilizers p=0.62 based on combined 5+15uM atlas e14 likely driven by the toxic 15uM well
Interpreted simultaneous tub_glcm_contrast +66.8 and act_glcm_contrast +41.7 at 15uM as tubulin bundling while ignoring parallel actin elevation indicating contraction artifact
Discounted replicated 1.5uM actin-dominant phenotype, e13 atlas with no stabilizer neighbours, second microscopist call of Actin disruptors, and weak mitotic dose response rho=+0.60 p=0.4
Failed to hypothesize Cholesterol-lowering until e20 and missed that statin HMG-CoA reductase inhibition explains actin phenotype via prenylation and Rho

citations.claim: Inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase depletes prenyl groups and thereby regulates intracellular actin polymerization.
HMG-CoA reductase inhibition with simvastatin prevents RhoA activation and downstream cytoskeletal to extracellular matrix signaling.
Statin effects on CTGF induction are Rho-dependent, supporting Rho-mediated actin cytoskeletal pleiotropy.
Statin pleiotropy prevents Rho kinase-mediated cytoskeletal barrier compromise.

reflection.next_experiment: Repeat lovastatin dose response with mevalonate plus geranylgeranyl-pyrophosphate rescue versus cholesterol-only rescue, imaging phalloidin actin and tubulin with RhoA membrane localization, alongside cytochalasin D, paclitaxel, and a statin reference panel controls.

## Reflection

I over-weighted the toxic high-dose acquisitions: the 15uM well with only 69 cells showing tub_glcm_contrast z=+66.8 together with act_glcm_contrast z=+41.7, and the combined 5+15uM atlas match to Microtubule stabilizers 7/10, and treated simultaneous tubulin and actin texture elevation as fibrillar bundling rather than contraction artifact. What was right:

- Failed to hypothesize Cholesterol-lowering until e20 and missed that statin HMG-CoA reductase inhibition explains actin phenotype via prenylation and Rho

Proposed next experiment: Repeat lovastatin dose response with mevalonate plus geranylgeranyl-pyrophosphate rescue versus cholesterol-only rescue, imaging phalloidin actin and tubulin with RhoA membrane localization, alongside cytochalasin D, paclitaxel, and a statin reference panel controls.
